probe: pinned /api/backends deferred routes: kobold generate (streaming, abort, error branches) and kobold transcribe-audio (multipart)

conventions.ordered: scenarios is an ARRAY and the replay MUST iterate it in order: every step shares ONE data root, and the transcribe 400 paths leave a staged upload behind, so step N sees what step N-1 left.
conventions.observation: each scenario is exchanged over a raw socket so the status, the FULL header list, the chunk framing and the terminator are observables; a fetch-based capture would decode all of them away
conventions.mock: body-URL peers are recorded as the <mock> marker and the pinned localhost-rewrite port as <port>; the Go replay substitutes its own local origin
conventions.outboundHeaderModel: explicitHeaders are the header object the route passed, lowercased and sorted; node-fetch 3 lowercases and SORTS them (node_modules/node-fetch/src/headers.js), so this is also the order they reach the peer relative to each other. Transport headers (Host, Connection) are not visible to the stub and are asserted on the Go side from nodeFetchWireDefaults instead.
conventions.multipart: the upload is built with a fixed boundary and recorded as a parsed part list; the real boundary is whatever the client sends, so the raw bytes are never compared
conventions.multipartParts: parts[].bytes and parts[].sha256 describe the value the PINNED server received, with the peer origin materialized; parts[].value is the same text with the <mock>/<port> markers restored, which is what the replay rebuilds and materializes against its own origin
conventions.uploads: the staging directory is recorded as [{name: '<upload>', bytes, sha256}] because multer's filename is random
conventions.frames: framing.frames are the chunked-transfer payloads in arrival order; framing.terminated reports the terminal zero-length chunk. A reply that is still open when the client disconnects has terminated:false.

nodeFetchWireDefaults.limitation: the stub sees the header OBJECT the route passed, before node-fetch adds its defaults, so a request with no body cannot show whether node-fetch would have added `content-length: 0`

derivedOnly.reason: UNREACHABLE, so no oracle exists. Both global body parsers run before any handler and body-parser 1.20.4 starts with `req.body = req.body || {}` (node_modules/body-parser/lib/types/json.js:108), so request.body is always an object by the time the route runs. Probed instead: a JSON body that omits api_server (kobold.generate.missingPrompt) reaches the handler with a body and no prompt. The Go handler reproduces the observable, not the dead branch.

UNREACHABLE through the pinned transport, so no oracle exists: the switch reads `error.status`, and node-fetch throws a TypeError/FetchError with no `status` member only on a transport failure, while an HTTP 403/503 is a resolved response that takes the non-ok branch. A transport failure therefore falls to `default` and answers {error:true} on the first attempt, which IS recorded (kobold.generate.transportFailure). The Go handler makes one attempt and answers the same; it does not implement a retry loop it cannot observe.

derivedOnly.branch: kobold/generate: a missing or non-string api_server
derivedOnly.reason: the pinned handler throws on `request.body.api_server.indexOf` inside an async handler with no try/catch and the process exits (the same crash the sibling /status row records). Not replayed against the pinned server, because it would kill the probe mid-wave. GoTavern answers 500, the documented deviation.

the pinned config keys `requestOverrides[].hosts/.headers` are not projected into HTTPHandlerOptions, so GoTavern applies no override headers. The scenarios set none, so every capture records the object with only content-type.

knownDifferences.status: crash and dead branches recorded, not reproduced
knownDifferences.reason: see derivedOnly: the body-parser guard and the 403/503 retry loop are unreachable, and a missing api_server exits the pinned process.
